newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen sidelined in grains/oilseeds market.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen sidelined in grains/oilseeds market.

text.p: Taiwan grains and oilseed importers are likely to go back to the sidelines after last week's buying spree in which they picked up 290,000 tonnes of corn and 122,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said on Tuesday.
"Buyers will take a break after active buying last week," said a U.S. trader based in Taipei.
The FGEP group, Taiwan's largest corn buying interest, bought 216,000 tonnes of U.S. corn on Friday in a move that caught traders by surprise.
"The group must have anticipated a corn futures rally" on the Chicago Board of Trade, a trader said.
Taiwan soybean buyers would also show little interest in the market this week since most of them have bought their nearby supplies, dealers said.
Wheat buyers were also expected to stay out since the island's near-term needs have already been filled.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $22.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments.
